title: Spotify companion rule set
description: STRUCTURAL PHASE ONLY. This schema encodes the grammar in rules-language.md -- the checks that, when they fail, reject the WHOLE rule set. It deliberately cannot encode the semantic phase: the field catalogue, which operators are valid for a given field's type, whether an operand matches that type, or the 32-level depth limit. A document this schema accepts can still load with individual rules DISABLED, each with a reason. Editor validation is a convenience, never the authority; src/rules/ruleValidator.ts is.

oneOf.description: Any member other than `rules` is ignored by the loader, including `version` and `$schema`.

id.description: Unique within the set. A DUPLICATE REJECTS THE WHOLE SET rather than disabling one of the pair: with two rules sharing an id, no report can say which matched. JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness across a keyed field, so this is unchecked here.

name.description: Display name. Not part of the rule's identity hash -- a rename does not change what the rule decides.

onUnknown.description: What to do when the rule's own verdict is `unknown`. WARNING: `hold` is accepted structurally but loads the rule DISABLED -- it needs a deadline and a re-evaluation trigger that do not exist yet.

dryRun.description: Optional, default false. Inert today: global automation is off, so every decision is dry-run regardless. A rule cannot opt OUT of a global dry-run.

field.description: Must name a catalogue field. NOT CHECKED HERE -- an unknown field loads the rule disabled with reason `unknown-field`. See rules-language.md section 2.

value.description: Required for every operator except `is-unknown`. `in` takes an array; everything else takes a scalar. Two things are NOT checked here because they are semantic: the operand's type must match the field's type, and an `in` array must be non-empty. Both disable the individual rule rather than rejecting the set.

then.description: `is-unknown` takes NO value. Writing `"value": null` is providing one, and is refused.

`in` requires an ARRAY structurally. That it must be NON-EMPTY is enforced in the semantic phase, so an empty array disables that one rule with reason `type-mismatch` rather than rejecting the whole set. Cross-checked against ruleValidator.ts -- do not add minItems here, it would make this schema stricter than the implementation and report a whole-file error for a single bad rule.

operands.description: MUST NOT BE EMPTY. An empty `and` is true and an empty `or` is false by the identity laws, but a rule containing one is almost certainly a mistake -- and the validator is a better place to object than an evaluator that invents an answer.
